> Abstract Clinical decision-making relies on identifying relevant patient information to guide diagnosis and treatment, a challenge that is especially difficult in the data-dense and rapidly changing intensive care unit (ICU). Large language models (LLMs) could support this task. However, existing applications and datasets mostly emphasize surface-level retrieval or factual recall rather than the inductive and deductive reasoning clinicians practice to select and reason over decision-relevant evidence. We hypothesized that training LLMs on expert ICU reasoning could yield clinical reasoning skills that generalize beyond critical care. Here we introduce ICU-REACT, a reasoning dataset developed with 19 clinicians through a clinician-in-the-loop framework to teach LLMs to perform information retrieval and context-aware clinical reasoning in the ICU. Using ICU-REACT, we fine-tuned Clin-REACT models spanning 8B-70B parameters and three model families. > Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) remain central to the assessment of clinical competence, yet the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into assessment design, delivery, and scoring raises a fundamental question: what evidence of competence are OSCEs intended to generate? This paper argues that AI should be evaluated through the lens of OSCE validity, with particular attention to how it may strengthen or weaken the interpretive chain linking observed performance to assessment decisions. Drawing on Messick's unitary conception of validity and Kane's argument-based framework, we examine how AI may introduce distinct threats across the scoring, generalisation, extrapolation, and implication inferences that underpin OSCE interpretation. We argue that generative AI (genAI) creates a particular risk of construct drift, whereby plausible assessment materials or scoring processes gradually reward observable proxies rather than the underlying clinical capabilities they are intended to assess. This randomized controlled experimental study compared the effectiveness of educator-guided and self-directed virtual patient training among paramedic students. Participants completed identical clinical scenarios using a virtual patient platform, either with real-time instructor support or independently with computer-generated feedback. Findings revealed that educator-guided training led to better performance across several domains of emergency assessment and management, especially in tasks requiring nuanced judgment and real-time decision-making. These results highlight the importance of instructional scaffolding and interpersonal feedback in simulation-based learning. In this Perspective, we describe Coach2Move, a person-centered approach aligned with the Age-Friendly Health Systems framework for older adults with mobility limitations and chronic conditions. > Organic chemistry occupies a contested place in pre-health education: required of nearly all premedical students, experienced as difficult, and justified on grounds that it “teaches you to think”, a claim too vague to evaluate or teach toward deliberately. Existing frameworks do not resolve this tension. This paper adopts a conceptual analysis approach, drawing on Ausubel's rote/meaningful learning distinction and the traditional transfer-of-learning literature, to propose impactful learning as a third pedagogical stage following rote and meaningful learning. Impactful learning is defined as the stage where procedural and reasoning skills exercised in mastering a discipline's content become generalizable cognitive tools deployable outside that discipline. Three key concepts are examined: the unit of transfer (the cognitive procedure, not the content), the extraction dimension (detachment of a practiced operation from the content that trained it), and the conditions under which such transfer becomes pedagogically achievable. > Medical professionalism has long been associated with rationality, emotional detachment, and self-control. Although often presented as universal standards of professional conduct, these norms are historically shaped by Western and individualistic epistemologies that frame emotions as threats to objectivity and ethical judgment. Such expectations shape Professional Identity Formation (PIF), often generating tensions between learners’ lived experiences and institutional norms. We argue that emotions are essential resources that qualify decision-making by helping us understand ourselves, the other, and the context, and anticipate the consequences of our decisions, thereby being essential for learning and professional identity formation. We draw on three decolonial perspectives. First, research on queer identities shows how trainees act as care weavers, transforming their own experience of marginalization into a relational capacity for empathy and clinical insight. > Background: Low back pain can restrict functioning through interacting symptoms, beliefs, and contextual demands. Qualitative inquiry can clarify how these influences are experienced. Objective: To explore perceived influences on disability and how they interact to restrict or support everyday functioning among adults with persistent low back pain. Methods: An interpretive qualitative study used purposive maximum-variation sampling to include 18 adults aged 25–66 years. Individual semi-structured interviews explored symptoms, movement, sleep, work, family roles, healthcare, and self-management. > Background Functional movement disorder (FMD) is increasingly being recognized as a condition associated with abnormal brain network connectivity; however, effective treatment strategies remain limited. Methods We report the case of a patient with severe FMD that developed following an occupational injury and was characterized by functional tremors accompanied by migraines and prominent autonomic symptoms. Based on electroencephalography (EEG) network analysis, low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area was administered, followed by staged rehabilitation incorporating visual feedback. Results The combined intervention reduced tremors and improved gait speed, activities of daily living, and EEG network connectivity. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Abstract This paper examines the impact of paid migrant home care on elderly health outcomes in Italy. The results show that an increase in migrants’ presence reduces both the frequency and duration of hospitalisations. Specifically, a 1 percentage-point increase in the migrant-to-elderly ratio leads to a decline in long-term and rehabilitation inpatient (LRI) admissions of 118 cases per 100,000 elders, with no measurable effect on acute inpatient stays. There is also a reduction in the average length of stay of 0.141 days, rising to 0.956 days for LRI cases. These effects are driven by diagnoses related to traumatic injuries, musculoskeletal, and genitourinary conditions — areas closely linked to home mobility and care management. Back-of-the-envelope calculations suggest that the average annual increase of 1.3 percentage points in the migrant-to-elderly ratio observed during the study period corresponds to an 8% reduction in elderly LRI hospitalisation costs, equivalent to 252.3 million euros.

> In response to national calls for a more representative health care workforce, this conceptual paper proposes the Model of Deliberate Occupational Therapy Practice (MDOTP), which aims to enhance pedagogical strategies related to supporting, engaging, and leveraging students’ unique cultural and experiential assets. Grounded in the scholarship of integration, authors draw from three theoretical frameworks, Funds of Knowledge, Therapeutic Use of Self, and Street-Level Bureaucracy, to provide a robust foundation for refining psychosociocultural approaches in occupational therapy education. After describing the MDOTP, a subsequent set of Guiding Principles (encourage reflective practice, development of the professional self, incorporate community-based learning, and promote collaborative learning environments) and corresponding action steps are provided to inform occupational therapy and allied health care curricula. Implications for future research and occupational therapy education are discussed.

> Managing hospital resources is a key strategic challenge in high-volume tertiary care, where turn-around time (TAT)—the time interval from the physician discharge order to physical. In this mixed-methods study of 320 inpatient cases in an Indian tertiary hospital, we utilize quantitative HIS time-stamp data and qualitative stakeholder perspectives to identify systemic bottlenecks. The results show that most discharges are timely, but a substantial proportion fail to meet benchmarks because of the administrative complexities brought by insurance-linked cases (TPA and PSU approvals), delayed billing processing, and logistical challenges. There was a significant temporal mismatch in late exit patients that resulted in them leaving at times when admissions are starting again in the early morning, which creates ED congestion and does not allow the most appropriate use of the beds (e.g., for patients being observed post-discharge). These demands may contribute to burnout-related experiences. This study assessed burnout among clinical optometry students at the University of Benin and examined the association between clinical supervision and burnout. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 150 clinical optometry students in 500 and 600 levels at the University of Benin. Participants were chosen using proportionate allocation and random sampling. Data were collected with a structured, self-administered questionnaire incorporating an adapted Maslach Burnout Inventory framework assessing emotional exhaustion, depersonalization and personal accomplishments, together with clinical supervision items. Data were analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 25.0. Frequencies, percentages and descriptive statistics were used, while Pearson chi-square tests assessed associations at a 5% significance level. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Leadership plays a decisive role in the implementation of inclusive education at the school level. In this paper, we report on a small-scale, qualitative study which explored how the beliefs and actions of leadership teams at two mainstream schools in the Maldives influenced their efforts to provide a shared vision for inclusion and a positive culture across their school community. School selection was based on purposive sampling, with both schools being recognised for their good inclusive practice. Semi-structured interviews with the six leaders (the principal, deputy principal, and the leading teacher at each school) were used to capture personal beliefs, shared understandings and daily actions that promoted inclusion at the respective schools. Data analysis revealed two major themes: Access for learning and Building collaboration and partnerships through supportive leadership. While a sense of duty, strong desire and personal drive were common threads running across individual perspectives and themes, leaders signalled that a lack of resourcing (human and material) was a major obstacle to the successful implementation of inclusive education in their country.

METHODS: A randomized controlled trial with three parallel groups: Pilates, Pilates + voluntary pelvic floor muscle contraction (Pilates + VPFMC), and PFMT was conducted. Method: This comparative cross-sectional study included 100 pregnant volunteers (50 educated, 50 non-educated). Data were collected using a structured questionnaire. This study investigates how different application rates of Guanoboost™ organic fertilizer influence nutrients and heavy metals dynamics in degraded soils. > An 80-year-old female with osteoporosis presented to the clinic in September 2026 reporting acute, severe, and spontaneous mid-to-lower back pain. Baseline dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) in April 2022 demonstrated a T-score of -3.0 at the femoral neck, -2.8 at the total hip, and -3.2 at the lumbar spine (L1–L4). She had no prior history of fragility fractures. She had received denosumab 60 mg subcutaneously every 6 months for 6 doses between April 2022 and April 2025 (total exposure 7 doses). She was lost to follow-up because she felt well and did not receive her scheduled dose in October 2025 or any subsequent antiresorptive therapy. Thoracolumbar radiographs were obtained (Figures 1 and 2).

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Jev has attracted considerable attention for its rapid, generalizable decision-making, yet its medical reliability remains under explored. To address this gap, our study compares various types of system-one decision models across 15 medical datasets comprising 8,742 instances under a unified protocol. Beyond accuracy, we assess decision stability and the ability to recognize unreliable decisions. Our results show that Jev rivals leading models on primarily text-driven tasks but is less effective on numerically driven tasks, revealing a distinct capability boundary. Under question-format variations, Jev demonstrates strong robustness, achieving the lowest decision reversal rate and relatively small accuracy fluctuations. Among evaluated open-source alternatives, only StartLux exhibits comparable robustness. But these strengths do not extend to reliable abstention awareness: most evaluated models show limitations in both recognizing missing correct answers and using optional abstention. Moreover, we find that Jev's probability-based answer selection can be improved by changing how decisions are scored: normalizing option-wise binary scores yields higher retained accuracy than choice...

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Large language model (LLM) assistants are being deployed to clinicians across health systems, and judgments about their readiness rest largely on benchmark scores, most of them derived from examination questions or curated cases. A benchmark predicts performance in deployment only to the extent that its items resemble real use, yet whether benchmarks reflect the work these systems receive has rarely been measured. Here we analyze 127,833 queries sent by 6,342 physicians, advanced practice providers and nurses in 35 specialties to an institutional assistant during an eight-month roll-out. We characterize each query with RCQ-Map, a clinician-validated framework grounded in taxonomies of clinical questions and of LLM evaluation, which records its task, intent, answerability, missing information and potential harm. Documentation and administration (36.2%) and knowledge retrieval (28.9%) made up nearly two-thirds of use, and diagnosis 3.7%; more than a third of queries could not be answered well as posed. The findings showed that occupational stress and burnout were commonly associated with high workload, long working hours, poor workplace and learning environments, inadequate supervision, limited autonomy, poor communication, mistreatment, and weak organisational support. > Background: Fascia has been overlooked throughout most of the history of anatomy, but many recent studies have begun to showcase its role. The ventral thigh has been extensively studied in various fields, including anatomy, biomechanics, physiotherapy, histology, and orthopedics. Therefore, the fascia lata is a good model for synthesizing the recent knowledge accumulated from studying this organ. Methods: A review was constructed to describe the characteristics of the deep fascia, with articles highlighting the main roles of the fascia lata selected for this purpose. Results: Forces travel through the fascia lata according to knee and hip positioning, optimizing energy sparing. When the knee is extended, the forces are transmitted to the iliotibial band whereas, when the knee is flexed, the forces are transmitted to the patella. Additionally, the fascia lata is a propri-oceptive organ. Its lengthening during a stretch is felt as pain while the mechanical tension is felt as a feeling of tension. > BACKGROUND: Autosomal recessive axonal neuropathy with neuromyotonia (ARAN-NM) is a distinct clinical and genetic entity within the hereditary peripheral neuropathies (HPN), caused by recessive loss-of-function mutations in the histidine triad nucleotide binding protein 1 (HINT1) gene. CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 13-year-old girl presenting with gait impairment and progressive motor weakness starting at the age of 6, with delayed muscle relaxation after a strong voluntary contraction, which developed later in the course. CONCLUSIONS: This case emphasises the elusive nature of ARAN-NM in children, whose clinical presentation is not distinctly characteristic at onset.

### Comparison of the centre of pressure movement variability between elite and non-elite wrestlers during a wrestling stance task

- **Auteurs** : مرتضی امانی, Mansour Eslami, Juan David Paucar Uribe, Daniel Rojas‐Valverde

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - Aucun mot-clé fort détecté

**Résumé / abstract :**

> This study compared the variability of centre of pressure (CoP) movement between elite and non-elite wrestlers during a repetitive wrestling stance task. Sixty male wrestlers (30 elite, 30 non-elite) performed a simulated 30 s protocol involving short-cycle repetitive wrestling stance tasks under two conditions: dominant and non-dominant leg. Non-linear Poincaré analysis was applied to the medial-lateral (ML) and anterior-posterior (AP) directions and to total (T) CoP displacement, computing short-term (SD1) and long-term (SD2) variability indicators. A mixed-model ANOVA with Bonferroni correction was used. Non-elite wrestlers showed significantly higher SD1 (p = .018) and SD2 (p = .008) in the ML direction of the dominant leg, whereas no differences appeared in the AP direction or in T displacement. Between legs, elite wrestlers differed significantly in SD1 (p = .008) and SD2 (p = .014) in the AP direction and in SD1 (p = .025) and SD2 (p = .039) of T displacement. No differences were found between the beginning and the end of the task. Poincaré analysis is a useful procedure for monitoring CoP movement variability during back-and-forth movements in wrestling.

> The aim of this qualitative descriptive research is to examine both the linguistic and discourse-level features of Medical English. The research employs a two-tiered approach: first, a linguistic analysis focusing on morphology, lexical density, syntax, and semantic evolution; second, a discourse analysis examining text organization, genre conventions, interactional patterns, and communicative practices. From a linguistic standpoint, Medical English is distinguished by its specialized terminology, extensive use of Greek and Latin roots, nominalized structures, passive constructions, and an expanding lexicon shaped by advances in numerous disciplines of Medical Sciences. At the discourse level, Medical English operates across multiple genres including clinical documentation, academic publications, and public health communication, each governed by established frameworks such as SOAP notes, IMRD structures, hedging strategies, and standardized phrasing in Medical research. As a result, Medical English has evolved beyond its traditional boundaries, emerging as dynamic and multifaceted domains of communication.

This review explores the relationship between diabetes and OH, covering its prevalence, pathophysiology, clinical implications, diagnostic approach, and management strategies. The pooled prevalence of OH across unselected diabetic populations is approximately 20–24%, notably higher than in the general population, and rises further among patients with established cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (CAN) or diabetic neuropathy. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Workplace ambiguity, where expectations, evaluations, or procedures are left unstated, acts as a structural access barrier for autistic and IDD workers, routinely forcing them to act on guesses. To investigate how these barriers operate, we interviewed 11 caregivers, concluding with an AI co-design activity to explore technological solutions. Their perspectives revealed five themes of workplace ambiguity, which we synthesize into a conceptual framework comprising three intersecting dimensions: evaluative, procedural, and relational. To address these barriers, participants proposed three forms of technology support, including ambient real-time redirection, feedback processing, and physiological guidance, designed to make hidden expectations perceptible and actionable. However, this exposes a core tension: technologies designed to make the workplace legible can inadvertently make the worker hyper-legible to employers through surveillance. We argue that ambiguity-aware workplaces must make expectations explicit before they carry consequences, and assistive technologies must remain accountable to the worker.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Professional identity crisis among medical students represents a major challenge in contemporary medical education. In this narrative review, we synthesize its multidimensional determinants and propose a three-stage developmental framework comprising academic burnout, professional identity erosion, and career withdrawal intention. These stages represent a progressive broadening of disengagement, from strain centered on medical training, to destabilization of the professional self, and ultimately to reconsideration of a future in medicine. We further organize intervention strategies at the individual, educational, and social/policy levels according to the major problems arising across these stages. By integrating previously fragmented evidence on burnout, professional identity, and career disengagement, this framework provides a conceptual basis for stage-informed intervention and a testable structure for future longitudinal research.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Academic burnout is a condition that students may experience due to continuous academic demands. One psychological factor related to students’ ability to cope with academic demands is self-compassion. This study aimed to determine the relationship between self-compassion and academic burnout among eleventh-grade students at SMA Negeri 5 Tasikmalaya. This study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational design. The population consisted of 502 students, with a sample of 223 students determined using the Slovin formula with a 5% margin of error and selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using the Indonesian Self-Compassion Scale and an academic burnout scale and were analyzed using Pearson Product Moment correlation. The results showed a correlation coefficient of -0.374 with p < 0.001, indicating a significant negative relationship of moderate strength. The coefficient of determination was 0.140, indicating 14% shared variation between self-compassion and academic burnout. Thus, higher self-compassion was associated with lower academic burnout. However, the correlational design does not establish a causal relationship.

This narrative review identifies two complementary documentation failures. The translation problem arises when symptom labels and intensity ratings do not capture effects on sustainable function, cognitive workload, emotional well-being, and participation. The fragmentation problem arises when specialties assess multisystem symptoms without preserving their temporal pattern, co-occurrence, shared triggers, treatment trade-offs, and recovery costs. ### Datasets for "Reporting Practices in Studies of Curriculum Integration in Medical Education: A Structured Narrative Review and Evidence Gap Analysis"

- **Auteurs** : wang xiao, yang yuanyuan, tan wenbin
- **Revue** : Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
- **Année** : 2026
- **Date de publication** : 2026-10-18
- **Source** : OpenAlex
- **DOI** : 10.5281/zenodo.23450649
- **PMID** : Non renseigné
- **PMCID** : Non renseigné
- **Lien** : https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23450649
- **Score** : 0
- **Décision** : **Faible priorité**
- **Tags proposés** : `#education_medicale`, `#sciences_education`

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **education_anchor** : medical education
  - **broad_review_penalty** : narrative review
  - **low_quality_or_repository_sources** : Zenodo
  - **source_penalty** : -10 points : dépôt, préprint ou source non prioritaire

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Datasets for a structured narrative review auditing the reporting practices of the curriculum integration literature in medical education. A PubMed search for studies of curriculum integration in medical education (executed 16 October 2026; entry dates from 1 January 2010) retrieved 405 records, of which 50 were excluded at the publication-type stage and 355 retained for secondary coding. Three files are provided:1. Supplementary_Dataset_coding_ALL_355.csv - per-record coding decisions for all 355 retained records, against two binary criteria (whether a retention, transfer or clinical-application outcome was measured; whether any processing-condition detail was reported).2. The research focused on teaching staff and student perceptions regarding the value of student diversity and the barriers that hinder academic performance. The approach was qualitative with a phenomenological design and included a sample of 10 university teachers and six students. The instruments used were a semi-structured interview guide for university teachers and a focus group guide for students. The data analysis procedure was conducted using ATLAS.ti (version 23). The results demonstrate a gap between the valuation of diversity and inclusive practice, whereby Universal Design for Learning (UDL) is not incorporated into session planning. Likewise, a lack of learning supports is recognised as a result of institutional deficiencies.

To further this scholarship, the current research represents a preliminary evaluation of the National De-escalation Training Center (NDTC) across several agencies and geographic regions of the United States. The study uses pre- and post-training data from over 500 trainees in the 6-month study period to determine if exposure to training informs changes to attitudes regarding procedural justice and de-escalation concepts. > Background: Colles' fracture, a fracture of the distal end of the radius, is among the commonest fractures of the upper limb, particularly in adults past the fourth decade of life. Its management in contemporary orthopaedic practice depends upon the degree of displacement and stability of the fragment, and ranges from closed reduction with immobilisation to operative fixation. Classical Ayurvedic surgical literature, most notably the Sushruta Samhita, describes a systematic approach to the management of fractures and dislocations under the heading of Bhagna Chikitsa, encompassing examination, reduction (Sthapana), stabilisation (Bandhana) and supportive care. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 54-year-old woman who presented with pain, swelling and deformity of the right wrist following a fall on an outstretched hand. Clinical and radiological assessment was consistent with a fracture of the distal radius. The patient was managed with supportive Bandhana (bandaging), local Taila application, Pata Sweda with hot water, Lepana with Ayurvedic formulations, and internal medication, with periodic reassessment and re-bandaging over the course of treatment. > Soil saline is one of the major abiotic stresses that severely reduced agricultural productivity as it imposes growth, nutrient and soil fertility constraints. This also reduces microbial diversity and, therefore, the nutrient cycle that is required for maintaining soil health. Recently, eco-friendly and sustainable salt-tolerant rhizobacteria have been developed to treat salinity stress. They promote plant growth by nitrogen fixation, phosphate solubilization, production of phytohormones, activity of ACC deaminase, exopoly saccharides synthesis and enhanced antioxidant defense. In addition to crop growth, soil conditioners promote the availability of nutrients through increased solubility and improved activity of soil micro-biota, all contributing to a more effective increase in soil quality. Plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) can mitigate or ameliorate salt-stress and give an eco-friendly sustainable approach against the use of synthetic fertilizers. We further summarize recent research efforts, possible applications so far, challenges and future prospects for utilization of these beneficial microorganisms in sustainable agriculture.

We introduce the concept of the “settlement-sphere”, which encompasses the physical, biochemical, and microbial microhabitat properties that govern successful coral larval recruitment. We then examine how anthropogenic stressors erode this settlement-sphere by diminishing essential chemical cues, reducing microhabitat complexity, and altering key physico-chemical conditions (e.g., hypoxia), ultimately leading to recruitment failure. > Animal-borne tri-axial accelerometers are increasingly used to investigate animal behaviour and energetics. Critical methodological details, such as device placement and dynamic range, are frequently underreported. This lack of reporting hampers study replicability and interpretation of results. It also complicates comparisons between studies. In addition, as device placement and attachment method can impact animal welfare and survival, transparent reporting should be considered vital for ethical publication. In this comment, we highlight these issues through a review of methodological reporting in studies involving attaching accelerometers to sea turtles. To address these challenges, we propose a framework for minimum standardised reporting that outlines key metadata which researchers should include when publishing studies utilizing animal-borne accelerometers. We also recommend thorough testing of devices and attachment methods prior to their use in the field. Adoption of this framework will enhance transparency, reproducibility, and comparability across studies, while promoting best practices in animal welfare. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Introduction: Posterolateral rotatory instability (PLRI) is the most common pattern of chronic elbow instability, typically resulting from inadequately treated elbow dislocations. Failure to recognize associated ligamentous injuries at the time of initial management can lead to persistent instability and progressive functional impairment. Case Report: We report a 46-year-old female who presented with persistent pain, instability, and restricted motion of the left elbow two months following closed reduction of an elbow dislocation. Clinical examination revealed positive PLRI tests on the affected side. Radiological assessment and intraoperative findings confirmed anterior radial head dislocation with complete disruption of both medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes. The patient underwent reconstruction of the collateral ligaments using a peroneus tendon autograft. The elbow was immobilized for three weeks postoperatively, followed by structured rehabilitation. Conclusion: Chronic PLRI requires a high index of clinical suspicion. Timely diagnosis and surgical reconstruction using tendon autograft provide reliable restoration of elbow stability and good functional outcomes.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> ABSTRACT This article advances a theory of co‐production as a relational state‐building strategy for countering youth radicalisation in fragile states. Grounded in fieldwork in northern Togo, affected by jihadist incursions from the Sahel and home to a predominantly young population, we argue that co‐production extends state presence into ‘brown areas’ and re‐legitimises authority by expanding the state's relational capacity to hear and respond to citizens. The framework specifies three interconnected mechanisms, face‐to‐face contact through service provision, civic inclusion via institutional channels, and the building of durable relational bonds, that jointly disrupt the recruitment pathways of extremist groups. Empirically, we show these mechanisms cultivate trust, dialogue and critical thinking among youth, while their structural reach is moderated by limited training and decision‐making authority. The findings reframe co‐production as a constitutive political force in state‐citizen relations, offering transferable insights for security policies across the Global South.

> Trustworthy biomedical AI requires reliable action selection when evidence is missing, stale, conflicting, or late, not only accurate answers on static inputs. We instantiate an episode-level evaluation protocol as 400 synthetic healthcare workflow episodes: 40 hand-authored semantic seeds across four task classes, two surface parameterizations, and five controlled variants, scored on ANSWER/ASK CLARIFICATION/ABSTAIN/ESCALATE under a pre-declared 5:1 missed-versus-unnecessary escalation cost. Reference actions are single-author study-policy labels, not clinician-adjudicated ground truth. Across five open-weight configurations (1.7B--9.7B), clean decision accuracy reaches 0.97, yet uncertainty-prompted models miss 32--97% of required escalations. The stronger 9.7B configuration narrows but does not remove the gap, falling from 0.97 clean accuracy to 0.78 under conflict. Verbalized confidence is inconsistent (ECE 0.10--0.54; failure AUROC 0.48--0.77), and a development-tuned confidence-only policy yields no utility gain. Surface morphology, phase constitution, composition, Raman features, and supporting surface characteristics were examined. Under dry sliding conditions, the CDHA-GNP-coated specimens exhibited lower specific wear rates than the untreated, oxidized, and CDHA-coated specimens for both Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-6Al-7Nb alloys. > Radiology reports, which document radiologists’ imaging observations and diagnostic conclusions from CT, X-ray and MRI scans, deliver core imaging evidence for clinical diagnosis and therapeutic planning. Inaccurate or disordered reports may lead to misdiagnosis and delayed intervention, posing risks to patient safety. Radiology reports are essential for clinical decision-making, yet Chinese radiology reports frequently exhibit logical inconsistencies, incomplete content, non-standardized descriptions, and formatting errors, while manual quality control remains time-consuming and inconsistent. Large teacher models can provide task-specific supervision but are difficult to deploy locally, whereas smaller models require adaptation to this clinical text task. We developed a teacher-supervised, locally deployable 4B language-model system for rule-based textual quality control of Chinese radiology reports. Among the three evaluated teacher APIs, Doubao-seed1.6-non-thinking achieved the highest macro-precision of 0.94, under the study’s precision-prioritized selection. > The article examines the content, structure, and major types of managerial competencies required in the education of family physicians within primary health care. Drawing on international competency frameworks and health professions education literature, it distinguishes organizational planning, clinical leadership, interprofessional coordination, communication, resource stewardship, quality improvement, and digital information management. The review identifies limitations of exclusively lecture-based instruction and discusses experiential approaches including workplace-based learning, simulation, case discussions, and reflective assessment. A competency-oriented educational framework is proposed to connect clinical decision-making with coordination of care and responsible use of health system resources. As a narrative review, the article presents a conceptual synthesis rather than original clinical or educational outcome data.

> Background Non-communicable diseases and injuries (NCDIs) constitute a leading cause of premature mortality globally, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). To curb the rising burden of NCDIs in Cameroon, the Ministry of Public Health established the National NCDI Poverty Commission to assess the burden of NCDIs, evaluate investments and expenditures related to NCDI services, and generate evidence to guide national policy formulation and resource prioritisation. Methods We synthesised data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2019 database and conducted a comprehensive literature review of peer-reviewed and grey literature (2005-2022) to characterise the burden and risk factors of NCDIs in Cameroon. > Magnetotherapy is an umbrella term applied to interventions that differ substantially in physical exposure, biological plausibility, and intended clinical effect. Static permanent magnets generate time-invariant fields, pulsed electromagnetic field (PEMF) devices generate time-varying low-frequency fields that induce electric fields in tissue, and repetitive peripheral magnetic stimulation (rPMS) uses higher-rate field changes to depolarise peripheral nerves and recruit muscle and proprioceptive afferents. Treating these modalities as interchangeable has contributed to inconsistent interpretation of the clinical literature. This critical narrative review evaluates their biophysical and biological mechanisms, clinical effectiveness, safety, dosimetry, and therapeutic implications. Literature published principally from 2000 to 2 August 2026 was identified through open scholarly sources, with earlier seminal work retained when necessary to interpret the field. We sought to evaluate the impact of a history of FFx on adverse postoperative outcomes following ≥ 3-level PSFs. Methods This retrospective cohort study queried the Mariner10 PearlDiver database to identify patients aged ≥ 50 years undergoing ≥ 3-level PSF for ASD from 2010 to 2022. All trauma, infection, and tumor indications were excluded. Patients with and without a history of FFx (hip, proximal humerus, distal radius, vertebral body, or pelvis fracture) were stratified. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with adverse outcomes (covariates: age, sex, CCI, obesity, FFx history). Results 439 ASD patients were identified, of which 33 (7.5%) had FFx. Las hormonas sexuales han sido señaladas como un factor clave, aunque no exclusivo, en estas diferencias. Esta revisión explora la evidencia sobre los factores que determinan las diferencias de sexo en la percepción del dolor. Métodos: Se realizó una revisión utilizando PubMed/MEDLINE (1 de enero de 2024). Tras la evaluación, 50 artículos cumplieron con los criterios y fueron incluidos. Resultados: Las mujeres presentan mayor frecuencia de dolor experimental y condiciones dolorosas crónicas como migraña, trastorno temporomandibular y osteoartritis. Las influencias hormonales, incluyendo los efectos duales de los estrógenos y la progesterona, y el papel potencialmente protector de la testosterona, parecen ser dependientes del contexto e insuficientes para explicar estas diferencias. This systematic review evaluated the efficacy, safety, methodological quality, and certainty of evidence for PBM in adults with TMD. Recent Findings This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251140804). PubMed, Embase, Scopus, LILACS via BVS, and MEDLINE via BVS were searched for randomized controlled trials published within the prespecified period from January 2015 to September 2025. **Résumé / abstract :**

> A 67-year-old woman with hepatocellular carcinoma developed acute right lower-extremity paresis and numbness immediately after adjunctive particle and liquid embolization of the right ninth through eleventh intercostal arteries and right inferior phrenic artery, followed by yttrium-90 transarterial radioembolization. Examination demonstrated severe right leg weakness with spared left leg strength, a right T10 sensory level with impaired ipsilateral vibratory sensation, asymmetric hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, and bilateral extensor plantar responses. Brain imaging and abdominal/lower-extremity computed tomography angiography excluded stroke and access-site injury. Although initial thoracic spine magnetic resonance imaging was read as normal, a neuroradiology addendum identified faint T2-weighted and short tau inversion recovery hyperintensity at T9–T10 and T11–T12, raising concern for acute spinal cord ischemia. Recovery remained limited at discharge. This case underscores the risk of spinal cord ischemia following extrahepatic collateral embolization and the importance of bedside neurological localization when early spine MRI appears normal.

> Many neck disorders, from chronic neck pain and headache to thyroid and nodal malignancy and radiation-induced fibrosis, both arise from and alter the mechanical properties of neck tissues, yet clinical assessment still relies on morphology, palpation and symptoms. Ultrasound and magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) now allow these properties to be measured in vivo, but the neck literature differs widely in methodology and remains dispersed across modalities and tissues. This review brings together the biomechanical basis of neck tissue behavior, the clinical conditions that alter it, and the principles and applications of ultrasound elastography and MRE in the neck. We show that ultrasound elastography has demonstrated diagnostic value for thyroid nodules and cervical lymph nodes, while neck MRE has been shown to be feasible but remains at an early stage. Across both modalities, reported values depend strongly on fiber orientation, posture, muscle activation and acquisition conditions. ### Síntomas y hábitos asociados a trastornos temporomandibulares en adolescentes de una unidad educativa de Ibarra, Ecuador

- **Auteurs** : Lady Andrea Quelal-Portilla, Jhojan Yair Noboa-Chávez, Gladys Viviana Urrego Cueva
- **Revue** : Sanitas. Revista arbitrada de ciencias de la salud.
- **Année** : 2026
- **Date de publication** : 2026-10-17
- **Source** : OpenAlex
- **DOI** : 10.62574/bscwfk36
- **PMID** : Non renseigné
- **PMCID** : Non renseigné
- **Lien** : https://doi.org/10.62574/bscwfk36
- **Score** : 0
- **Décision** : **Faible priorité**
- **Tags proposés** : Aucun tag proposé

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - Aucun mot-clé fort détecté

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Objetivo: describir la frecuencia autorreferida de síntomas y hábitos asociados a los trastornos temporomandibulares en adolescentes escolarizadas. Método: estudio transversal en 95 estudiantes de 14 a 15 años de décimo año de Educación General Básica de una unidad educativa de Ibarra, Ecuador, seleccionadas por conveniencia. Durante una jornada educativa se aplicó un cuestionario de cinco preguntas cerradas y se calcularon frecuencias y porcentajes. Resultados: el 48,4 % refirió dolor mandibular al masticar o hablar, el 38,9 % ruidos articulares, el 38,9 % rigidez mandibular, el 36,8 % bruxismo del sueño y el 44,2 % apoyar la mano en la mandíbula. Conclusión: los síntomas y hábitos asociados a estos trastornos son frecuentes en esta población y justifican la evaluación clínica y la educación preventiva escolar.

**Mots-clés détectés :**

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is a progressive disease characterized by expiratory flow limitation, whose main symptom is dyspnea, which limits exercise capacity in patients with the disease, resulting in pulmonary functional alterations and muscular skeletal dysfunction. The main risk factor that predisposes the disease is smoking and the senile population is the hardest hit. Objective: To observe the effects of respiratory muscle training in COPD patients. Methods: Articles were reviewed using the MEDLINE, SCIELO and LILACS databases, articles published in the last 5 years (2015/2025) in Portuguese and English. Discussion: The results showed that inspiratory muscle training was more beneficial in individuals with inspiratory muscle weakness, however strength training helped in increasing endurance and muscle strength. Conclusion: Inspiratory muscle training is an important marker for the treatment of COPD by improving lung function, thus benefiting the quality of life of individuals, while physical training did not have definite evidence for improvement in lung function but tolerance to pulmonary function and yes exercise tolerance and muscle strength.

Nevertheless, hyperacute timing should not be regarded as an absolute contraindication to TEVAR. In patients with rupture, malperfusion, impending aortic rupture, persistent pain, refractory hypertension, or progressive true-lumen collapse, prompt entry-tear coverage can restore perfusion and prevent irreversible organ injury. This skewness reflects competition for attention, whereby most publications are gradually forgotten and only a minority continue to be recalled years later. Exploiting this observation, we construct a researcher-level indicator based on authorship of top 10% cited papers in All Science Journal Code (ASJC) bins and apply it to publications affiliated with Irish institutions over a typical funding cycle. Restricting attention largely to original research papers, we find that researchers authoring strictly more than one ASJC top-decile paper in a given year exhibit persistent participation in the highly cited tail of the literature in subsequent years, thus the simple track record indicator possesses predictive value. **Résumé / abstract :**

> We present an active inference account of persistent dizziness predicated on models of enactivism and ecological psychology; including first-hand accounts of the patient’s lived experience. Mechanistically, we consider persistent dizziness to reflect an initial failure of sensory attenuation of vestibular and other sensory prediction errors. This failure becomes self-maintaining if the patient infers—or learns—that unattenuated prediction errors cannot be resolved through action. The ensuing formulation provides an integrative account of the pathophysiology of dizziness and how it underwrites—and is maintained by—affective inference and an altered sense of agency that shapes the experience of the person with dizziness. We foreground the holistic person-centered approach on offer from a clinical perspective, and consider complementary levels of therapeutic intervention under this theoretical framework.

These structural inequities contribute to persistent disparities in pain prevalence, pain-related disability, and opioid utilization. Telemedicine is a promising strategy for reducing this access gap, with adoption accelerating markedly following the COVID-19 pandemic. This narrative review examines telemedicine for chronic pain management in rural populations across synchronous video visits, telephone-based encounters, asynchronous electronic consultations, telerehabilitation, tele-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy, and mobile health applications. The evidence base is strongest for remotely delivered cognitive behavioral therapy and selected telerehabilitation interventions, whereas evidence for specialty video programs, electronic consultations, Veterans Health Administration programs, and mobile health remains more heterogeneous and frequently observational. Where age is a major risk factor, occupational and ergonomic exposures contribute to spinal degeneration. Repetitive biomechanical loading and heavy lifting may accelerate degenerative changes. This narrative review aims to understand the dose- response relationship between occupational and ergonomic factors, development of cervical and lumbar spondylosis, while evaluating dose-response patterns that are associated with pharmacological, rehabilitative and ergonomic interventions. A narrative review of available literature was conducted on occupational risk factors, ergonomic determinants, cumulative biomechanical loading, pathophysiological and therapeutic strategies related to cervical and lumbar spondylosis. Evidence related to exposure intensity, frequency, duration and treatment outcomes were synthesized. İkinci bölüm, tanı ve cerrahi tedaviden sağkalım sürecine kadar olan aşamaları kapsayacak şekilde, mesane kanserinde bütüncül hemşirelik bakımının temel bileşenlerini incelemektedir. > Arthritis is one of the leading causes of chronic pain, disability, and reduced quality of life worldwide, affecting millions of individuals through progressive joint inflammation, cartilage degeneration, and bone destruction. Although conventional therapies, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), glucocorticoids, disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), biologics, and Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors, effectively alleviate symptoms and delay disease progression, their long-term use is frequently associated with adverse effects, high treatment costs, and incomplete disease remission. Consequently, phytotherapy has emerged as a promising complementary and alternative therapeutic strategy owing to its multitarget pharmacological actions and comparatively favorable safety profile. This review comprehensively summarizes the current knowledge on the pathophysiology of arthritis, emphasizing inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and major intracellular signaling pathways, including NF-κB, MAPK, JAK/STAT, PI3K/Akt, NLRP3 inflammasome, COX-2, and 5-lipoxygenase. Antropometrik ölçümler, kardiyorespiratuvar uygunluk değerlendirmeleri, kas kuvveti ve dayanıklılığı testleri, esneklik, denge ve çeviklik ölçümleri ile laboratuvar temelli fizyolojik ve biyomekanik yöntemler çocukların fiziksel kapasitesinin ayrıntılı olarak değerlendirilmesine katkı sunmaktadır. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Background: Evans syndrome (ES) is a rare autoimmune disorder defined by concurrent autoimmune haemolytic anaemia and immune thrombocytopenia, some patients also developing autoimmune neutropenia. Pulmonary complications are seen only rarely, and the underlying mechanisms are not well defined. Case Presentation: We describe a 44-year-old male with ES since 2025 who presented with four months of breathlessness, dry cough and fever. HRCT of the thorax showed bilateral ground-glass opacities with areas of cavitation and consolidation. Bronchoscopy and microbiological work-up returned no infectious cause. As the patient continued to deteriorate, a trans-thoracic lung biopsy was performed. Histopathology confirmed diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) consistent with acute lung injury, with no evidence of fungal, viral or granulomatous infection. The patient was treated with corticosteroids, immunomodulatory therapy, and broad-spectrum antimicrobials along with supportive care.Conclusion: This case highlights a rare but severe pulmonary manifestation of Evans syndrome. Diffuse alveolar damage should be considered in ES patients presenting with unexplained respiratory failure.

> High-resolution neuromuscular ultrasound (US) is a valuable tool for the localization, diagnosis, and provision of conservative treatment to peripheral entrapment mononeuropathies. US-guided interventions require careful coordination of transducer and needle movement along with a detailed understanding of sonoanatomy. Preprocedural planning and positioning are instrumental in performing these interventions and should not be overlooked. Minimally invasive procedures, such as corticosteroid injections, aspiration of ganglia, orthobiologics, and hydrodissection, are useful options for the nonsurgical treatment of mononeuropathies refractory to conservative care. Although cycling is frequently prescribed during rehabilitation, the effects of pain on bilateral cycling biomechanics remain poorly understood. This study investigated experimentally induced movement-evoked knee pain on bilateral torque and power output, inter-limb asymmetry, and inter-individual motor responses during cycling. Twenty-three healthy adults (14M and 9F) completed an incremental cycling test followed by eight randomized constant-load trials under pain and no-pain conditions at two intensities. A custom closed-loop torque-dependent electrical stimulation system induced movement-evoked knee pain during the downstroke while bilateral biomechanics were recorded. At higher intensities, movement-evoked knee pain reduced torque (p=0.026, d=0.566) and power (p=0.010, d=0.657) production in the painful limb and altered the normalized symmetry index (NSI) for power (p=0.005, d=0.659), and torque (p<0.001, d=0.754). Pichotka, Lisa Heß, Thomas Reinheckel, Gerd Strohmeier, Behnam Shamshiri, Sebastian Lucas, Maxim Zaitsev, Alexander Maier, Laura Adela Harsan, Caroline Bund, Jan-Bernd Hövener, Leif Schröder, Andreas B.   - **negative_keywords** : cancer, breast cancer

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Hyperpolarized 13 C-MRI enables real-time imaging of metabolic conversions in vivo, but remains largely restricted to specialized sites with superconducting high-field MRI and polarization infrastructure. Here we present a broadly deployable method for preclinical hyperpolarized 13 C-metabolic imaging, which combines signal amplification by reversible exchange (SABRE), a parahydrogen-based hyperpolarization technique, with detection of [1- 13 C]pyruvate-d 3 in a compact 436 mT permanent-magnet small-animal MRI system. SABRE yields 13 C-pyruvate polarization of 13% at ~30 mM in a purified, biocompatible solution, with a T 1 relaxation time of 140 s. In a transgenic breast cancer mouse model, 13 C-chemical shift imaging after injection resolves pyruvate, pyruvate hydrate and lactate in vivo, maps elevated lactate-to-pyruvate ratios in mammary tumors and images three freshly prepared pyruvate doses sequentially in the same animal in less than one hour. This compact SABRE-to-low-field method makes repeated hyperpolarized 13 C-metabolic imaging mobile and accessible in standard preclinical research environments.

The combination of these immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with conventional treatments demonstrates significant synergistic potential. Standard oncological regimens often center on chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, or various combinations thereof. This synergy stems from complementary mechanisms: conventional therapies can induce immunogenic cell death, release tumor antigens, and remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, thereby laying the groundwork for immunotherapy. > Between 1938 and 1941, nearly 20,000 Jewish refugees fleeing Nazi persecution arrived in wartime Shanghai, a city already destabilized by the Sino-Japanese War (1937-1945), mass displacement, and fragmented governance. Their arrival exposed the limits of Shanghai's overstretched public health system while also generating new forms of medical organisation, refugee self-governance, and intercultural collaboration. Drawing on archival records, refugee memoirs, wartime newspapers, and medical journals, this article reconstructs the development of an improvised yet integrated refugee healthcare infrastructure between 1939 and 1945. The article argues that refugee medicine in Shanghai evolved beyond emergency relief into a broader regime of care comprising hospitals, nutrition programmes, sanitation campaigns, disease surveillance, and work-relief initiatives. **Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **negative_keywords** : pediatric

**Résumé / abstract :**

> BACKGROUND: Spontaneous chronic spinal subdural hematomas (cSSDHs) are a rarely reported clinical pathology in pediatric patients in which subdural blood accumulates without an obvious etiology. OBSERVATIONS: The authors report 2 cases of pediatric patients with cSSDHs with no known nonaccidental trauma, coagulopathy, or underlying vascular malformation. The patients presented with progressive back pain and paresthesias. Both cases were treated successfully with decompression and evacuation of subdural blood products using a posterior short-segment laminectomy (case 1) or laminoplasty (case 2), which yielded satisfactory improvement in pain and no recurrence through follow-up. LESSONS: Chronic SSDHs are not always associated with an underlying vascular malformation or coagulopathy. Posterior decompression and evacuation of blood products can yield satisfactory outcomes without early recurrence. Spontaneous spinal subdural hematoma should be a diagnosis of exclusion after thorough workup to rule out potentially underlying etiologies of the pathology. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26105.

> ABSTRACT This paper provides a notion for the use of electroencephalography (EEG) in the field of cognitive science. In particular, we investigated the brain activity of operators while spotting the differences in similar‐looking pictures at three levels of difficulty. As many practical loads are fundamentally intrinsic, the task was designed to specifically induce intrinsic workload (the productive load as per Cognitive Load Theory (CLT)). The experiment used the task: Spot the Difference to create a workload scenario comprising three difficulty levels: spotting five differences, three more differences, and two more differences (along with retaining the previous differences from working memory). The task was designed intrinsically as the operators are generally occupied with tasks involving working memory and requiring attention towards the varying number of resources. By utilising the brain signatures a mental workload model was developed employing a Support Vector Machine (SVM) as the classifier. Four anti-HER2 antibodies, trastuzumab, pertuzumab, trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1), and trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), were profiled with integrated ERBB2 mRNA data. On antigen-oriented arrays, cell-synthesized HER2 bound trastuzumab and pertuzumab strongly and epitope-dependently, whereas wheat-germ HER2 showed no binding. On the tissue lysate array, trastuzumab and T-DM1 bound HER2-positive cancer cell lines and tumor tissues with nearly identical profiles (correlation coefficient r = 0.991), and T-DXd bound ERBB2-low cancer spots and 38.8% of normal human tissue spots, a profile not conserved in cynomolgus monkeys. Trastuzumab, T-DM1, and pertuzumab showed no cross-reactivity with cynomolgus monkey tissues, whereas T-DXd bound 3.1% of monkey tissue spots. NexAb enables quantitative cross-reactivity profiling relevant to preclinical safety evaluation.

### Effect of alternate nostril breathing exercise on blood pressure in hypertensive patients: a literature review

- **Auteurs** : Mistati Novitasari, Lia Novita Sari, Hasrita Octaliana
- **Revue** : Media Keperawatan Indonesia

- **Lien** : https://doi.org/10.26714/mki.9.3.2026.290-301
- **Score** : 0

- **Tags proposés** : Aucun tag proposé

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **strong_study_design** : randomized controlled trial
  - **broad_review_penalty** : literature review
  - **negative_keywords** : pharmacological

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Hypertension remains a major health problem in Indonesia. Hypertension is also known as the primary cause of cardiovascular disease, which contributes to a high mortality rate. One of the non-pharmacological approaches to managing hypertension is the alternate nostril breathing exercise to reduce systolic and diastolic blood pressure by modifying the rise and fall of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve function. The purpose of this literature review is to determine the effect of alternate nostril breathing exercises on reducing blood pressure in hypertensive patients. The literature review method used three databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect) and was analyzed using the PICOT strategy. The journals used had a quasi-experimental, pre-experimental, and randomized controlled trial design published between 2019-2024. Based on the 5 journals that have been reviewed, it was found that alternate nostril breathing exercise affects reducing blood pressure in hypertensive patients, both systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Therefore, alternate nostril breathing exercises can be applied as a non-pharmacological therapy for hypertensive patients.

Método: estudio cuantitativo, descriptivo y transversal. Se aplicó un cuestionario estructurado en línea a 47 padres seleccionados por conveniencia en febrero de 2025. Resultados: el 72,3 % refirió que sus hijos se cepillan tres o más veces al día y el 66,0 % supervisa siempre el cepillado. Solo el 30,4 % informó uso diario de hilo dental; el 48,9 % acude al odontólogo cada seis meses y el 31,9 %, solo ante un problema. El 91,5 % consideró muy importante la higiene bucal. Conclusión: la higiene se valora mucho, pero persisten brechas en limpieza interdental, supervisión y control preventivo.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Objetivo: analizar la relación entre el tiempo de cepillado dental y la eficacia en la remoción de placa bacteriana. Método: revisión narrativa de 15 artículos publicados entre 2009 y 2024 en revistas indexadas en PubMed que abordaron la duración, técnica y tipo de cepillado, la supervisión y el control químico de la placa. Resultados: un cepillado de dos minutos elimina más placa que uno de un minuto, aunque una sola sesión retira menos de la mitad. Los adultos sin instrucción se cepillan poco tiempo. Los cepillos eléctricos, la supervisión parental y la educación mejoran el control de placa. Los colutorios solo complementan la acción mecánica. Conclusión: el tiempo de cepillado es necesario, pero insuficiente si no se acompaña de técnica, instrumento adecuado y supervisión.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Objetivo: analizar la evidencia que compara la eficacia de los cepillos dentales eléctricos y manuales en la higiene bucal. Método: revisión narrativa con búsqueda en PubMed y SciELO de revisiones sistemáticas, ensayos clínicos y estudios clínicos en español o inglés; se analizaron 15 documentos. Resultados: las revisiones sistemáticas y los ensayos clínicos mostraron que los cepillos eléctricos, sobre todo los oscilantes-rotatorios, eliminaron más placa y redujeron más la gingivitis que los manuales, con diferencias modestas. El beneficio se observó en niños, adolescentes y personas con discapacidad, pero no fue consistente en pacientes con ortodoncia fija. Ambos fueron seguros para los tejidos. Conclusión: el cepillo eléctrico ofrece una ventaja moderada; la elección debe individualizarse según la destreza, las necesidades clínicas, el costo y la adherencia.

> Background UV photofunctionalization has been proposed as a method to enhance implant surface bioactivity and potentially improve early osseointegration. Objective This study aimed to evaluate early implant stability under early loading conditions by analyzing changes in Implant Stability Quotient (ISQ) values over time. Methods This case series included three implants placed in the posterior mandible and treated with UV photofunctionalization for 24 hours prior to placement. Implant stability was assessed using Resonance Frequency Analysis (RFA) at baseline (implant placement), at 3 weeks, and at 4 weeks prior to functional loading. Insertion torque values were recorded at the time of implant placement. Results A progressive increase in ISQ values was observed across all cases, ranging from 77 to 85, with no evidence of a stability dip during the study period. Conclusions Within the limitations of this case series, the observed ISQ progression indicates a favorable stability pattern under early loading conditions. However, due to the small sample size and absence of a control group, no definitive conclusions can be drawn regarding the specific effect of UV photofunctionalization.

Although cranial ultrasound is widely used as a bedside screening tool, brain MRI has become central to diagnosis, injury pattern classification, timing estimation, and outcome prediction. Furthermore, proton MR spectroscopy ( 1 H-MRS) provides complementary metabolic biomarkers that enhance prognostication. This review focuses on MRI and 1 H-MRS in neonatal encephalopathy due to hypoxic–ischemic injury, addressing both term and preterm infants. The pathophysiologic determinants of injury distribution are summarized, the optimal timing of imaging and diffusion evolution is discussed, and practical acquisition protocols including recommended sequences and 1 H-MRS parameters are proposed. Key MRI phenotypes in term infants—basal ganglia–thalamus injury, watershed/parasagittal cortical–subcortical injury, and global or near—total injury patterns are reviewed with attention to common pitfalls such as diffusion pseudonormalization and evolving T1/T2 signal changes. Here, we present the results of a nationwide survey of university students, conducted by the Education Group of the Italian Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, from more than 2000 students across 49 academic institutions in Italy, with the aim of capturing not only which learning resources are relied on but also the underlying motivations for their choices and perceptions of biochemistry.
